drivingQuestion: Does Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's condition qualify the mishna's first clause or Rabbi Yehuda's clause?
outcomeNote: Two versions of where the qualification attaches are recorded without deciding; the difference between them is drawn out in the next unit.

segments.he: עַכְבָּר שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ [וְכוּ׳]. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: וְהוּא שֶׁהִשְׁרִיץ עַל פְּנֵי כּוּלּוֹ. אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַסֵּיפָא – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּאֲדָמָה שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד בָּשָׂר טָמֵא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: וְהוּא שֶׁהִשְׁרִיץ עַל פְּנֵי כּוּלּוֹ.
segments.en: §The mishna teaches: In the case of «a mouse that» grows from the ground and «is half-»flesh half-earth, one who touches the half that is flesh is impure. «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says» in this regard: One becomes impure in such a case «only» if the flesh of the mouse has «developed along the entire» length of the mouse, from head to foot. «Some teach» the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi «with regard to the latter clause» of the mishna: «Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who touches» the half that is «earth where it is adjacent to the flesh is ritually impure. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:» One becomes impure in such a case «only» if the flesh of the mouse has «developed along the entire» length of the mouse.

moves.summary: The Gemara re-quotes the mishna's clause about the half-earth mouse.
moves.about: quoting the mishna's clause about the mouse that is half flesh and half earth

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: והוא שהשריץ על פני כולו
moves.summary: He qualifies the first clause: only where the flesh formed along the mouse's whole length.
moves.about: the first clause's ruling that touching the flesh half imparts impurity holds only where the flesh has formed along the mouse's whole length

moves.summary: A second version attaches the same qualification to Rabbi Yehuda's clause instead.
moves.about: recording that some attach Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's qualification to the mishna's latter clause rather than to its first
